# Tasks

This is the team's shared task board. The PM creates entries; every agent updates the
status flag for the tasks it touches. This file is the single source of truth for work
state — the `/shell-team:run` loop advances the flag at each phase gate.

## Status flags

`READY_FOR_ARCH` → `READY_FOR_ENG` → `READY_FOR_QA` → `READY_FOR_REVIEW` → `READY_FOR_MERGE`
(or `BLOCKED` / `REWORK` at any stage)

Branch `feature/1056-loop-liveness`; PR base `develop`. This branch is **stacked three deep** — on T-1055's tip, which is on T-1054's, which is on T-1053's — so the merge base is `develop`'s tip and all three earlier tasks' delivered paths are already changed against it through no act of this task.
  - the deliverable, in one sentence: four new files — `bin/check-liveness.sh` (a fail-closed classifier read out-of-band by a timer this task does not ship, emitting exactly one bare token on stdout — `RUNNING` / `WAITING` / `STALLED` / `DEAD` / `OBSERVE_ERROR` at exits 0/3/4/5/2 — from a closed 19-token refusal set), `tests/check-liveness/run.sh`, `templates/liveness-reasons.txt` (the closed 8-row reason vocabulary a declaration draws from) and `templates/prompt-blocks/liveness-declaration.md` (the write/clear norm authored once, registered `contain` against both skills) — plus one registry row, one choke-point paragraph appended to each of `skills/run/SKILL.md` and `skills/goal/SKILL.md`, CI wiring and a test-recipe append. **Nothing consumes the verdict**: no transport, no daemon, no loop gate, no board write.
  - **the design decisions worth stating on the board**: (1) **exit `1` is assigned to no verdict at all** — bash's own `errexit` fallback is 1, so a contract that used it could not distinguish "decided this" from "crashed before deciding", and a behavioural assertion over it would be structurally vacuous. (2) **`STALLED` and `DEAD` are not separated by a distinction of kind, and the spec says so** — nothing in already-persisted state, read read-only, reports whether a process is alive, and the issue rules out the loop writing its own heartbeat. What separates them is a second threshold **plus a second quantity**: `DEAD` requires the tick clock *and* the last-commit clock both past `T_dead`, so it is strictly stronger than a bigger number on one clock. (3) **The board's active flags are declined as a matrix dimension and read by nothing** — a flag names which phase a task is in, never whether anything is executing, so classifying on it would repeat the stillness-as-alarm error the issue rejects one level up; the classifier resolves no board path. (4) **A missed deletion cannot pin `WAITING` forever** — the failure mode that would make the artifact worse than nothing is closed structurally rather than by discipline: a declaration whose `run-epoch` differs from the run's `start_epoch` is refused, and one whose `declared-epoch` is not later than the state file's mtime is *superseded* (the loop demonstrably ticked since the wait was declared) and falls through to the ladder, whose `RUNNING` cell independently requires that same recent mtime.
  - **DP4's omission class is closed by a mechanism, not a sweep**: 17 human-hand-off points across the two skills are enumerated with line numbers in the spec, and rather than 17 individual edits the design is **one choke point per skill plus one closed reason vocabulary**, with `bin/check-prompt-sync.sh` enforcing that neither surface drifts from the canonical block and a two-directional set equality enforcing that no skill invents a reason the classifier will refuse and no registry row exists with no writer.
  - **pre-commitment, with the drop order and the never-dropped set both named before round 1**: factual trigger = two consecutive rework rounds of new independent `Blocker`/`Major` findings against one component; contextual trigger = a third round about to start; **the factual trigger governs when they disagree**. **Never dropped**: the four-value classification core (each value reachable and generated by real observation) and the fail-closed matrix (one verdict per cell, `RUNNING` only on positive evidence and never a fallthrough default). If a round's findings would require **weakening** either, the task **stops and returns to sprint planning** rather than being patched — it is not silently dropped and no third droppable is invented to avoid the stop.   - **the two design decisions worth stating on the board, both measured rather than assumed**: (1) **`bin/team-paths.sh` gains no key.** The config resolves as `<base>/binding.conf` composed from `--get base`, exactly as `bin/check-durability.sh` composes `<base>/durability-mode`. Measured ground: `tests/team-paths/run.sh:154-171` pins the resolver's key set at exactly ten in both directions and its own comment records T-1006's AC2 as having raised that pin from nine, so an eleventh key reddens that pin and the merged criteria behind it for a benefit nothing needs — the epic makes the config read-only to every agent, so no prompt-injected path is required. AC3 locks this as a negative criterion. (2) **the hash covers the canonical resolved binding, not the config's bytes** — a comment reflow, a row reorder or a CRLF conversion does not stop the loop, while any bound value change does. This deliberately narrows "a change is mechanically detected" to the property #203 actually protects; a stop triggered by a comment edit is a false stop that trains its reader to ignore it.

The load-bearing half is not the directory: the lock records the config path it was taken from and `--verify` **never re-resolves** that path, so a base directory resolving differently in a later phase is reported as `path-mismatch` instead of quietly followed.   - the decisions, in brief (D1–D10, full text in the spec's `### Settled decisions`). **D1 — the key is `<file>:<content>` and the judgment is declared count against measured count**, one mechanism producing both directions (`comm -23` forward, `comm -13` reverse) exactly as today. The alternative was rejected on a **measured decoy, not on taste**: a set difference over *deduplicated* content keys absorbs a second byte-identical unguarded line in the same file silently, which is strictly weaker than the position keying it would replace. An occurrence-index key reintroduces a position-like field that reorders on deletion; an anchor+content key needs an anchor that is a position pin under another name. **One derivation constraint is load-bearing**: the raw derivation keeps `grep -n`'s line numbers **through** its `sort -u` and strips them only when the key is formed — dropping the field earlier collapses two byte-identical sites at the source and no downstream count can recover them.   - the round-1 repair, in brief: **matchability is qualified rather than promised** — a merge SHA always matches, a pull-request number matches **only where the merge subjects actually carry one** (a merge-commit workflow writes it there, a squash or rebase workflow does not; stated that way to stay adopter-neutral), and a task ID **never appears in a sub-bullet at all** and is repositioned as the label the framing maps a SHA or PR number *from*, never a token the agent matches. Task IDs are **not** narrowed out of the Input space's framing-side list — the two texts are reconciled honestly instead, with a task-IDs-only framing declared a **reachable** input whose defined behaviour is the `## Notes` route. **Whole-window coverage is now part of the requirement**: every returned sub-bullet must end up matched to the cycle's own material or explicitly flagged as foreign, and the `## Notes` disposition now covers **both** failure modes (no matchable material, **and** any unaccounted or foreign entry). The `pr-metadata` stream is deliberately **not** joined to the reconciliation — it is optional and `gh`-auth-gated, so joining it would breach the fetch-nothing constraint that keeps the norm satisfiable in an adopter's repository. AC3's pins are regrouped into four labelled element groups and now carry the two **revert-detection locks** for exactly this Major (restoring the three-equivalent-identifiers list; deleting the coverage clause), so a later "simplification" back to the v1 reading turns AC3 red even where AC1/AC2 byte equality would stay green.

  - task classification, stated so review rigour is calibrated rather than guessed: **verification-mechanism work, lightweight variant** — it writes a new checker (a parity harness), the class the playbook says runs long, but it is black-box, test-only, adds no parsing of a text format, and changes no shipped behaviour.   - D1–D6 settled in the spec: (1) **the common oracle** — the two consumers do not observe alike (`bin/cluster-failures.sh` surfaces a row only when it is a FAILING span, so a clean probe makes every cluster-side assertion vacuously green), therefore every probe row carries `"status":"error"` and the two frozen outcomes are `counted` (rollup `spans: 1` AND cluster `count=1`) and `skipped` (rollup exactly `(no runs found)` AND cluster exactly `(no failure clusters found)`), with the event probe deliberately a hybrid row so a wrongly-counted event is observable on both sides; (2) a **dedicated suite** `tests/is-span-row-parity/` with its own fixtures (repo convention), a shared cross-suite fixture dir rejected, plus a mechanical single-source invariant over the probe marker and the six basenames; (3) **black-box only** — no `sed`+`eval` extraction exists to fail closed, and the suite must resolve both scripts through `$REPO_ROOT` rather than `PATH` or the mutation criteria cannot go red; (4) the **six classes** of issue #80, one row per file, with the five `kind-*` fixtures identical once the `kind` field is deleted so a classification difference is attributable, and `tests/*/fixtures/with-events.jsonl` as the source of the real event-row spelling; (5) a divergence names the drifted script and the fixture; (6) CI registration (shellcheck arg list + own `run:` step) plus a `## Appended by tasks` recipe entry.
  - known boundary, declared rather than discovered: if BOTH copies receive the same patch, parity holds and the parity half cannot see it. - [x] **T-1011** Run telemetry gains event rows alongside spans — `READY_FOR_MERGE` — spec: .shell-team/specs/T-1011-telemetry-event-rows.md
  - closed: 2026-08-01, PR #81 → develop — issue #77 stays open (Parts 2/3 = T-1012)
  - source: GitHub issue #77, **Part 1 only** — "extend run telemetry with event rows". No separate issue was filed: #77 already carries all three parts and stays the tracker, and Part 1's scope is quoted verbatim into the spec's Problem section so the split is auditable against the issue rather than against this board line. Parts 2 and 3 (`bin/gen-loop-replay.sh`, `templates/loop-replay.html`, README/docs wiring) are T-1012. Base `develop` at `08ebaea`, branch `feature/77-part1-telemetry-events`, PR body carries `Closes #77` only when Part 3 lands — this PR references #77 without closing it.
  - why it exists: telemetry records one thing, a span per sub-agent call. Every transition *between* the calls — a phase hand-off, a route-back, a gate verdict, a human stop or GO, a release — leaves no row, so a run log reads back as a bag of agent invocations rather than as a sequence of what the loop did. Part 2's replay needs the transitions; no inference over span rows reconstructs "a human stopped the loop here". The row shape has to exist first.
  - task classification, stated so review rigour is calibrated rather than guessed: this **writes and extends a verification mechanism itself** (`bin/check-run.sh` is the validator; `bin/log-run.sh` is the only writer and calls the validator in a post-write self-check). Per this repository's playbook that is the long-running class, not the pure-addition class — spec-review rigour is set at the higher standard and a multi-round rework is the expected shape, not a surprise.
  - resolved for the engineer (D1): event rows go in the **same** `<loop_id>.jsonl`, and **both** raw-row consumers learn to skip them. The consumer inventory is measured, not assumed — `grep -c field_str bin/*.sh` returns exactly two files, `bin/rollup-runs.sh` (11) and `bin/cluster-failures.sh` (5); `bin/rollup-track.sh:121` consumes rollup-runs' *stdout* and `bin/retro-inputs.sh:455` only counts `.jsonl` files, so both are outside the blast radius by measurement. **Rejected, with the measurement that kills it**: a `<loop_id>.events.jsonl` sidecar — `agents/triage-orchestrator.md:33,52,76` documents invoking both consumers as `<runs>/*.jsonl`, so a `.jsonl` sidecar is swept into that glob and corrupts them exactly as if it were in the same file, while additionally costing Part 2 a two-file merge. **Also rejected**: the implicit-skip variant (omit `run_id`/`status`/`verdict` so today's consumers ignore event rows untouched) — it genuinely works today (`rollup-runs.sh:77`, `cluster-failures.sh:114`) and is rejected anyway, because replay must group by `run_id` and a skip that happens by accident of field absence is the silent-corruption class the decision exists to remove. The skip rule is **fail-safe**: `kind` absent or `span` is a span, anything else is skipped — an unknown `kind` is by definition not a span, and reporting it is the checker's job, not the reporters'. Neither consumer gains any new output (a new `events: N` line would change a git-tracked `rollup-track.sh` artifact and `consolidate-proposals.sh`'s input).
  - resolved for the engineer (D2): the discriminator is a `kind` key whose **absence means span**, so span rows stay byte-identical (17 keys, same order, no `kind`) and no existing file is invalidated. Closed enum `span|event`; `"kind":"span"` is accepted and validated as a span; any other value, `null`, or unquoted fails closed. Shape mixing is a violation **both** ways: an event row carrying any of the **13 span-only keys**, or a span row carrying `event`. The reverse check is on `event` alone — it is the discriminator's partner key and can mean nothing else, whereas `from`/`to`/`label` are generic enough for a future span-side extension and fall under the tolerated-unknown-key rule. All new event-side key detection is **object-boundary anchored**, reusing `bin/rollup-runs.sh:60`'s precedent; the existing span-side `REQUIRED_KEYS` detection is left byte-identical because changing it would be a span-side behavior change.
  - resolved for the engineer (D3): the vocabulary is issue #77's proposal adopted verbatim as a closed enum — `handoff|rework|gate|human|release` — and the row is exactly 9 keys in a frozen order, with `loop_id`/`run_id`/`seq`/`ts` shared with spans and `seq` a **single monotonic per-run counter across both shapes** so Part 2's replay has a total order. Per-id requiredness is frozen in a table in the spec (handoff: from+to; rework: from+to+label; gate: from+label; human: label; release: none), each `label`-required row justified by the field carrying the event's whole informational content. `from`/`to` stay free-form — an adopter's phases are not this loop's phases.
  - resolved for the engineer (D4): the checker's enforce/tolerate split is enumerated, and **seven reason strings are frozen** so every negative criterion is greppable (`invalid event '<v>' (handoff|rework|gate|human|release)`, `event must be a quoted enum value`, `missing required event key(s):` — deliberately distinct from the span side's wording — `event '<id>' requires non-null <field>`, `event row carries span-only key(s):`, `span row carries event-only key: event`, `invalid kind '<v>' (span|event)` / `kind must be a quoted enum value`). Tolerated and out of contract to flag: unknown extra keys, nullable fields absent or `null`, arbitrary `label`/`from`/`to` text, trailing whitespace, CRLF, blank lines. Structure: `REQUIRED_KEYS` stays the span array byte-identical, the event side gets its own sets, `lint_line` runs the shape-independent checks first and then branches — and the event branch never runs the span required-key/status/verdict checks, because an event row is not a defective span.
  - resolved for the engineer (D5): `--event <id> [--from X] [--to Y] [--label L]`. All **13** span-only flags are usage errors in event mode (exit 2, nothing written) rather than being left for the post-write lint to catch, mirroring D2's mixing rule 1:1; `--event` with `--span` carries the frozen message `--event and --span are mutually exclusive`; `--from`/`--to`/`--label` are usage errors in span mode; an unknown `--event` value and an empty-string required value are usage errors. Version skew (new writer × old checker → row written, exit 1, never rolled back) is **confirmed and re-affirmed rather than redesigned** — it is what the header already documents for every self-check failure, every caller wraps the call in `|| true`, and telemetry is best-effort by contract; it must be written into the header instead of left to be rediscovered.
  - resolved for the engineer (D6): only `skills/run/SKILL.md`'s Telemetry section changes, with each event id mapped to a point where a span is already emitted (`handoff` at the phase boundaries, `rework` at both route-back points, `gate` at the QA/Codex verdicts plus the fail-closed seam gates, `human` at stop/GO/interrupt using the existing `interventions-classes.md` slugs as the recommended label vocabulary, `release` at close-out), alongside the `|| true` and shared-`seq` rules. **Rejected**: per-step reminders through steps 1–7 — one instruction copied seven times is the drift surface `CLAUDE.md` warns about.
  - resolved for the engineer (D7): the shape discrimination stays a **flat single-line scan; no grammar-aware tool is adopted**. Grounds: `bin/` is pure-bash zero-dependency by contract, so `jq`/python is unavailable in an adopter's repo; and the invariant needs no grammar state — every check is a per-line key test, and `log-run.sh`'s `jesc` guarantees no bare `"` inside a value, so a boundary-anchored key token cannot occur inside a string. The residual (a hand-forged escape sequence) is declared out of scope in the Input space rather than left implicit.

The event vocabulary is added to `tests/machine-tokens/run.sh` (same class as every other token group there) and proved to bite by mutation. **Parallel telemetry surfaces dispositioned up front rather than discovered later**: `skills/goal/SKILL.md` and `skills/review-response/SKILL.md` are untouched with stated reasons and locked as a protected invariant, so "you missed a parallel surface" is answered by the frozen intent instead of costing a round.

  - **DP-b modifies the tech-lead's recommendation, on the authority of the canonical issue text.** The recommendation was "a `Superseded-by` target must share the superseded entry's `Scope`". #23's stated reason for one file is that splitting "would make a local lesson that generalises unable to name its universal replacement — an un-retirable class" — i.e. `maintainer → loop` supersession is a design requirement, and a symmetric rule would forbid it. The rule adopted is **directional**: only `loop` superseded by `maintainer` is rejected (the graph stays healthy while a shipped rule vanishes with nothing replacing it in the shipped set); `loop→loop`, `maintainer→maintainer` and `maintainer→loop` stay legal. ## Format

```markdown
- [ ] **T-XXX** <one-line title> — `<STATUS_FLAG>` — spec: <specs-dir>/<slug>.md
  - <optional latest note from whichever agent touched it last>
```

`<specs-dir>` is `.shell-team/specs/` by default (or `docs/specs/` in a legacy
`tasks/` layout). The hand-off linter accepts any spec path ending in `.md`.
